spot_story_tteunbongsaem.title: Tteunbongsaem Spring, Source of the Geumgang River
spot_story_tteunbongsaem.subtitle: 10-18 Mulppuraengi-gil, Jangsu-gun (Geumgang Love Water Experience Center)
spot_story_tteunbongsaem.pull_quote: Where King Taejo Yi Seong-gye witnessed a mythical phoenix soaring on a five-colored rainbow and received the omen to found the Joseon Dynasty — the very headwaters of the Geumgang River flowing 397.25 km to the West Sea.
paragraphs: Ascending 1.5 km along the valley of Sinmusan Mountain in Subun Village brings you to Tteunbongsaem Spring, the ultimate source of the Geumgang River. Legend tells that King Taejo Yi Seong-gye, founder of the Joseon Dynasty, offered prayers here and received a divine revelation to establish the new dynasty after seeing a phoenix rise into the sky atop a rainbow.

From this quiet spring, the stream journeys 397.25 km all the way to the West Sea estuary. The surrounding Tteunbongsaem Ecological Park features the Geumgang Love Water Experience Center, native wildflower colonies, an eco-playground, an ecological greenhouse, and forest trails. Showcasing endangered species, amphibians, and reptiles, it offers visitors enriching ecological education and memorable outdoor experiences.

spot_story_deogyusan.title: Deogyusan National Natural Recreation Forest & Giant Norway Spruce Trail
spot_story_deogyusan.subtitle: 530-62 Gucheondong-ro, Mupung-myeon, Muju-gun
spot_story_deogyusan.pull_quote: Beneath soaring, majestic Norway spruces reaching toward the sky, immerse yourself in the serene, deep breath of the forest across all four seasons.
paragraphs: Nestled beside Deogyusan National Park and Gucheondong Valley, Deogyusan Natural Recreation Forest offers deep woodland relaxation throughout the year: vibrant royal azaleas in spring, crystal-clear streams in summer, fiery autumn foliage on Jeoksangsan Mountain, and breathtaking rime frost with snowy vistas in winter.

The recreation forest is densely populated with Japanese larches and Korean pines, alongside its signature highlight: a magnificent Norway spruce forest planted in 1931. Soaring gracefully toward the heavens with an exotic, grand ambiance, the gentle woodland trails allow anyone to enjoy a rejuvenating phytoncide walk.

spot_story_baengnyeonsa.season_badge: 🌺 Early Winter to Spring Camellia Grove · Path of Contemplation

spot_story_baengnyeonsa.title: Gangjin Mandeoksan Baengnyeonsa Camellia Forest & Dasan Trail
spot_story_baengnyeonsa.subtitle: 145 Baengnyeonsa-gil, Doam-myeon, Gangjin-gun (Natural Monument No. 151)
spot_story_baengnyeonsa.pull_quote: An 800-meter woodland trail where Dasan Jeong Yak-yong and Master Hyejang strolled to share tea and philosophy, embraced by 1,500 native camellia trees.
paragraphs: Surrounding the historic Baengnyeonsa Temple—where Venerable Wonmyo organized the White Lotus Society during the Goryeo Dynasty—thrives a lush forest of around 1,500 indigenous camellia trees designated as Natural Monument No. 151. Beginning to bud as crisp winds arrive in late autumn and early winter, they carpet the tranquil path with crimson blossoms well into early spring.

Passing through a 7-meter-high camellia canopy toward Dasan Chodang thatched house, this serene hillside path is where renowned scholar Dasan Jeong Yak-yong walked daily during his exile to meet Master Hyejang. Along this path of contemplation, visitors are treated to panoramic views overlooking the placid waters of Gangjin Bay.

spot_story_cheongnyeongpo.title: Yeongwol Cheongnyeongpo Cape, King Danjong's Forest Surrounded by Water
spot_story_cheongnyeongpo.subtitle: Gwangcheon-ri, Nam-myeon, Yeongwol-gun, Gangwon (Scenic Site No. 50)
spot_story_cheongnyeongpo.pull_quote: A secluded inland island accessible only by boat; ancient pine groves and the majestic Gwaneumsong tree quietly witnessing a young king's tragic exile.
paragraphs: Located along the winding Seogang River in the upper reaches of the Namhangang River, Cheongnyeongpo Cape is surrounded by deep water on three sides and flanked by the sheer cliffs of Yukyukbong Peak to the west. Accessible solely by ferry, this naturally secluded sanctuary is where King Danjong, the 6th monarch of the Joseon Dynasty, was exiled after his dethronement.

Stepping off the short ferry ride, visitors are welcomed by a dense pine grove carrying centuries of history and the venerable Gwaneumsong Pine Tree (Natural Monument No. 349). Ascending to Manghyangtap Pagoda and Nosandae Cliff, the tranquil currents of the Seogang River blend with autumn leaves and pine fragrance, leaving a deeply resonant impression.

spot_story_suncheonman.title: Suncheonman Bay Wetland, Golden Reed Fields Swaying in the Sunset Breeze
spot_story_suncheonman.subtitle: 513-25 Suncheonman-gil, Suncheon-si (UNESCO World Natural Heritage)
spot_story_suncheonman.pull_quote: Korea's premier ecological garden where hooded cranes soar over endless golden reed waves and the S-shaped tidal channel glows in evening crimson.
paragraphs: Gently cradled by the Goheung and Yeosu peninsulas, Suncheonman Bay is an expansive coastal wetland spanning over 75 km². From autumn through winter, vast colonies of tall golden reeds sway like shimmering silver waves, creating a magnificent spectacle.

Strolling along the barrier-free wooden boardwalks accessible to strollers and wheelchairs, visitors can observe thriving mudflats brimming with crabs and mudskippers. An easy climb up to Yongsan Observatory unveils an unforgettable sunset descending across the iconic S-shaped waterway.

spot_story_jusanji.subtitle: Jusanji-ri, Juwangsan-myeon, Cheongsong-gun, Gyeongbuk (Scenic Site No. 105)
spot_story_jusanji.pull_quote: A mystical mountain reservoir built in 1721 that has never dried up, weaving a watercolor morning of submerged King Willows and ethereal water mist.
paragraphs: Completed in 1721 during the reign of Joseon King Gyeongjong, Jusanji Reservoir rests atop dense welded tuff formations formed from volcanic ash. For over 300 years, this enchanting mountain pond has never run dry or exposed its bottom, even through the severest droughts.

In the early morning when delicate mist drifts low across the water, over twenty centuries-old King Willows rooted deep in the lake cast serene reflections upon the mirror-like surface, quietly drawing photographers and travelers year-round.

Within the urban regeneration project in Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province, house repair support projects are conducted to improve living environments by renovating old houses, along with training and qualification courses for residents to maintain and manage improved environments according to local conditions.

This event introduces personnel who practice sharing in the community by improving neighbors' living environments using the skills learned through such training. Major programs include home repair experiences, woodworking workshops conducted by repair experts and professional training organizations, special lectures on preparing for house repairs, lectures on managing vacant houses, demonstrations of cleaning techniques, and house repair consultations. spot_ev_4151224.overview: 'Learning History Together' is a participatory historical and cultural program that explores Jeonju's historical and cultural heritage with family, based on the 'Wanyeong Ilrok', a record of the daily life and work of Seo Yu-gu, the governor of Jeolla during the Joseon Dynasty. Participants will visit major historical and cultural sites such as Jeollagamyeong, Yeodamgo, Wanpan Cultural Center, Jeondong Catholic Church, and Pungnammun Gate, examining historical backgrounds with professional guides, viewing artifacts, and experiencing excavation, woodblock printing, and pansori performances.

spot_ev_3396705.title: Ulsan Cultural Expo
spot_ev_3396705.overview: The 2026 Ulsan Cultural Expo is a comprehensive cultural festival under the slogan 'My Ulsan, Our City', sharing the process of how the daily lives and stories of each citizen come together to form the culture of the city. With the UNESCO World Heritage designation of 'Bangudae Petroglyphs' in July 2025, Ulsan is gaining attention as a city where ancient history and modern culture coexist. Just as prehistoric people engraved their lives on rocks, today's Ulsan citizens are also carving the culture of the city in their own ways.
spot_ev_3396705.pull_quote: Seasonal recommended festival in Ulsan Ulju-gun Samnam-eup · UECO (2026.11.26 ~ 2026.11.29)

With the UNESCO World Heritage designation of 'Bangudae Petroglyphs' in July 2025, Ulsan is gaining attention as a city where ancient history and modern culture coexist. Just as prehistoric people engraved their lives on rocks, today's Ulsan citizens are also carving the culture of the city in their own ways. This year's expo focuses on the flow of individual cultures starting from 'My Ulsan' to a shared asset called 'Our City'.

The core value of this expo is 'Cultural Governance for Mutual Growth'. Citizens, local cultural artists, cultural enterprises, universities, and public institutions participate together from planning to operation, creating a cultural space that is collaboratively built rather than a one-sided exhibition. spot_at_2373363.title: Lee Jae-myung's Place of Action
spot_at_2373363.overview: Lee Jae-myung's Place of Action is where the young activist Lee Jae-myung attempted to assassinate the pro-Japanese traitor Lee Wan-yong on December 22, 1909. As Lee Wan-yong arrogantly passed by in a rickshaw, Lee Jae-myung lunged at him with a dagger, shouting 'Long live Korean independence!' He was captured and fatally injured by the police's swords, dying on September 30, 1910. To honor Lee Jae-myung, a commemorative stone was installed by the city of Seoul.

spot_at_1605966.title: Hunryeonwon Park
spot_at_1605966.overview: This site was once the training ground for soldiers, where martial arts training and military formations were taught. Established in 1392 during the reign of King Taejo of Joseon, it was initially called the Training Hall. Later, during King Taejong's reign, it was moved here, and a large hall for archery practice and military examinations was built. It was renamed Hunryeonwon in 1466.
spot_at_1605966.pull_quote: This site was once the training ground for soldiers, where martial arts training and military formations were taught.
paragraphs: This site was once the training ground for soldiers, where martial arts training and military formations were taught. Established in 1392 during the reign of King Taejo of Joseon, it was initially called the Training Hall. Later, during King Taejong's reign, it was moved here, and a large hall for archery practice and military examinations was built. It was renamed Hunryeonwon in 1466.

Before the current Hunryeonwon Park and parking lot were built, there was a wooden structure decorated with red bricks, made from timber transported from Baekdusan along the Amnok River to the Yellow Sea. The wood recovered during the demolition was processed to create this information board, preserving the historical essence. The park opened on June 30, 1997, featuring landscaped facilities such as lawns, drinking fountains, and mist fountains, along with management offices, restrooms, and benches.

spot_at_129534.title: Tapgol Park
spot_at_129534.overview: Tapgol Park is the first modern park in Seoul, built on the site of the Won-gak Temple during the Joseon Dynasty. Established in 1397, it was transformed into a park by British advisor Brown in 1897 and officially opened in 1920. It is historically significant as the site where the Declaration of Independence was first read during the March 1st Movement in 1919.
spot_at_129534.pull_quote: Tapgol Park is the first modern park in Seoul, built on the site of the Won-gak Temple during the Joseon Dynasty.

Established in 1397, it was transformed into a park by British advisor Brown in 1897 and officially opened in 1920. It is historically significant as the site where the Declaration of Independence was first read during the March 1st Movement in 1919.

On May 28, 1992, the park's name was changed from Pagoda Park to Tapgol Park. The park features cultural heritage sites such as the National Treasure 10-story stone pagoda of Won-gak Temple, the 3·1 Movement Memorial Tower, murals commemorating the 3·1 Movement, and statues and memorials for independence activists.

The mountain is also called 'Yeoksan' because it turns its back on Hanyang.

spot_at_1942237.title: Old Baekje Hospital, Busan
spot_at_1942237.overview: The Old Baekje Hospital is the first modern private general hospital building in Busan, serving as an important medical institution alongside Busan Municipal Hospital and Railway Hospital. According to the National Heritage Portal, the building was formed by combining two structures built in February and December 1927. After the hospital closed, it was used for various purposes, including a Chinese restaurant, Japanese military officer's quarters, Busan Police Headquarters, the Republic of China’s temporary embassy, and a wedding hall. After a fire in 1972, the fifth floor was demolished, and it currently stands as a four-story building.

spot_at_126028.title: Geumjeongsan Mountain
spot_at_126028.overview: Geumjeongsan National Geopark is a mountain formed by granite that solidified from magma underground about 70 million years ago, serving as the root of Busan's land. Visitors can admire the elegant granite formations shaped by years of wind and rain, including cliffs, tors, inselbergs, and block streams. spot_at_126028.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partner · Nearby Restaurants & Safe Accommodation Routes
paragraphs: Geumjeongsan National Geopark is a mountain formed by granite that solidified from magma underground about 70 million years ago, serving as the root of Busan's land. Visitors can admire the elegant granite formations shaped by years of wind and rain, including cliffs, tors, inselbergs, and block streams. The main peak, Godangbong, along with Janggunbong, Wonhyo-bong, and Sanghakbong, has fortresses built along the ridges connecting these peaks.

These peaks and ridges feature unique tors, which are exposed remnants of large and small bedrock from the Cretaceous Bulguksa granite. The geology of Geumjeongsan consists of sedimentary rock layers from the Gyeongsang Group and volcanic rocks that intruded or erupted through them, along with the Bulguksa granite and Masan granite that intruded into these rocks. Registered as a national geopark, Geumjeongsan boasts beautiful scenery where bizarre rock formations and nature harmoniously coexist.

spot_at_975899.pull_quote: Local recommended partner · Nearby restaurants and safe accommodations
paragraphs: Located in Dong-gu, Old Dongchon Station began operations as a regular station in 1917 and was in service until 2008. It is the best-preserved station among the old Daegu Line stations and has retained much of its original 1930s architecture, earning it a designation as a registered cultural heritage site. The station features a wooden structure with a unique 'ㅅ'-shaped ceiling in the waiting room, and the design of the large gable of the waiting room and the small gable of the office is distinctive, allowing for clear visibility of the platform. Old Dongchon Station is architecturally significant due to its sharp gable roof design.

On May 15, 2008, the old Daegu Line was officially closed, and Old Dongchon Station was shut down along with Banya-wol Station. On April 1, 2014, Dongchon Park was established on the site of the old Daegu Line, and Old Dongchon Station was relocated and restored from Geomsa-dong in Dong-gu. Since May 17, 2014, it has been utilized as the 'Dongchon Station Small Library'. The park preserves part of the old railway tracks that were at Dongchon Station and has created an exhibition space within the Old Dongchon Station building.

spot_at_2746368.title: 2·28 Memorial Central Park
spot_at_2746368.overview: 2·28 Memorial Central Park was established to commemorate the 2·28 Student Democratic Movement. Opened in June 2003, it covers an area of 14,354㎡. The 2·28 Student Democratic Movement, which occurred in 1960, was a student-led protest in Daegu against the corrupt Rhee Syng-man regime, serving as a catalyst for the 3·15 Masan Incident and the 4·19 Revolution that ultimately led to the fall of the Rhee government. The park is located on the site of the former Daegu Central Elementary School, where traces of the 2·28 movement remain.

spot_at_128814.title: Ganghwa Samrangseong
spot_at_128814.overview: Samrangseong, located in Gilsang-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, was a fortress built to defend Kaegyeong and Hanyang since the Goryeo Dynasty. The circumference is about 2.3 km, and the fortress follows the terrain of the mountain from the summit to the southern gate at an elevation of 75m, resulting in a significant height difference between the north and south. The three sons of Dangun were assigned to build each peak of Jeongjoksan, and people named this mountain fortress Samrangseong using the character for 'young man' (郞). It is also known as Jeongjoksanseong, located at an elevation of 222m south of Ganghwa Island.
spot_at_128814.pull_quote: Local Recommended Partners · Nearby Restaurants · Safe Accommodation Routes
paragraphs: Samrangseong, located in Gilsang-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, was a fortress built to defend Kaegyeong and Hanyang since the Goryeo Dynasty. The circumference is about 2.3 km, and the fortress follows the terrain of the mountain from the summit to the southern gate at an elevation of 75m, resulting in a significant height difference between the north and south. The three sons of Dangun were assigned to build each peak of Jeongjoksan, and people named this mountain fortress Samrangseong using the character for 'young man' (郞). It is also known as Jeongjoksanseong, located at an elevation of 222m south of Ganghwa Island.

The exact date of construction is unclear, but it is estimated to have been built using rough natural talc, a technique from the Three Kingdoms period. In 1739 (15th year of King Yeongjo), the southern gate was rebuilt, and a gate tower was constructed, named Jonghaeru. It was again repaired in 1764 (40th year of King Yeongjo). In 1866 (3rd year of King Gojong), it was the site where Yang Heon-soo's troops defeated the French army. Inside Samrangseong is Jeondeungsa, the oldest temple in Korea and the largest temple in Ganghwa.

spot_at_1620578.title: Janggot Dondae
spot_at_1620578.overview: Janggot Dondae, located in Janghwa-ri, Hwado-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon, is a fortification from the late Joseon period. It was designated as an Incheon Metropolitan City monument on March 2, 1995. Along with Migot Dondae, Bukilgot Dondae, and Geomam Dondae, it is part of Janggot Fortress. Large-scale fortifications were constructed for coastal defense from the reign of King Hyojong to King Yeongjo, most of which were built in 1679 (5th year of King Sukjong). King Sukjong mobilized 8,000 soldiers from Hamgyeong, Hwanghae, and Gangwon provinces and 4,300 soldiers from the Royal Guard to build 49 fortifications in just 40 days.

spot_at_1953948.overview: Hyanggyo is an educational institution established by the state to honor the spirits of sages and conduct rituals, while also educating local citizens. Built in 1127 on the northern side of Hwacheong Mountain, it was relocated to its current site in 1741 and renovated in 1966. It is said that An Hyang brought a statue of Confucius from Yuan Dynasty on his way back from China in 1286, leading to the establishment of Confucian shrines in various towns in Seoul.

Built in 1127 on the northern side of Hwacheong Mountain, it was relocated to its current site in 1741 and renovated in 1966. It is said that An Hyang brought a statue of Confucius from Yuan Dynasty on his way back from China in 1286, leading to the establishment of Confucian shrines in various towns in Seoul.

The remaining buildings include Myeongnyundang, which serves as an educational space, and Daeseongjeon, which is the ritual space, along with Dongmu and Seomu. Additionally, there are inner and outer gates and a ritual offering storage. During the Joseon Dynasty, it received land, slaves, and books from the state to educate students, but after the Gabo Reform in 1894, its educational function ceased, leaving only the ritual function. spot_at_127575.title: Mudeungsan National Park (Gwangju)
spot_at_127575.overview: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢ and is located in the northern and eastern districts of Gwangju, as well as in Damyang-gun and Hwasun-gun. The park is primarily composed of various types of rocks including Hwasun andesite, Mudeungsan tuff (quartz andesite tuff, Mudeungsan basalt, quartz andesite), Dogok volcanic rock, Mimu granite, biotite granite, quartz porphyry, and dike rocks.
spot_at_127575.pull_quote: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢...
paragraphs: Mudeungsan was designated as a provincial park on May 22, 1972, and was designated as the 21st national park on March 4, 2013. Mudeungsan National Park covers an area of 75.425㎢ and is located in the northern and eastern districts of Gwangju, as well as in Damyang-gun and Hwasun-gun. The park is primarily composed of various types of rocks including Hwasun andesite, Mudeungsan tuff (quartz andesite tuff, Mudeungsan basalt, quartz andesite), Dogok volcanic rock, Mimu granite, biotite granite, quartz porphyry, and dike rocks.

The most notable feature of Mudeungsan is its columnar jointing. Columnar joints are formed when high-temperature lava cools on the surface, resulting in polygonal columns. These columnar joints can be well observed in the Mudeungsan columnar joint area (Seoseokdae, Ipsukdae, Gwangseokdae), Gyubong Rock, and Jungbong. Particularly, the highest peak of Mudeungsan, Cheonwangbong, at an elevation of 1,187m, features vertical jointed rocks that rise dramatically, resembling a stone wall. The rock formation known as Saeinbong, named for its resemblance to a jade seal, is located on the western ridge of Jangbuljae and consists of a curtain-like rock cliff.

spot_at_1330521.title: Chungjangno
spot_at_1330521.overview: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno. Chungjangno was the main north-south road connecting the South and North Gates during the city wall era and was referred to as the city center. The commercial area on Chungjangno began to form shortly after the Japanese colonial period in 1911 when a Japanese national opened a general store called 'Yeomok' across from the current Industrial Bank.

paragraphs: If Myeongdong exists in Seoul, Chungjangno exists in Gwangju, Jeonnam. As the city expands, many new bustling streets have emerged, but the center of Gwangju will always be Chungjangno. Chungjangno was the main north-south road connecting the South and North Gates during the city wall era and was referred to as the city center.

The commercial area on Chungjangno began to form shortly after the Japanese colonial period in 1911 when a Japanese national opened a general store called 'Yeomok' across from the current Industrial Bank. After that, shops owned by Japanese nationals began to appear around Chungjangno 1-ga, and the reason they could dominate the commercial area was due to the presence of the Japanese Governor-General's office at the former provincial government site. The name 'Chungjangno' is derived from the posthumous title of Kim Deok-ryeong, a general during the Imjin War. The first streetlights on Chungjangno were oil lamps. Historically, it has been a hub for clothing, suits, and food services, attracting many young people and becoming known as a street of trends and youth.

spot_at_1621360.title: May 18th Democracy Square
spot_at_1621360.addr: 38 Munhwa Jeondang-ro, Dong-gu, Gwangju, South Jeolla Province
spot_at_1621360.overview: May 18th Democracy Square is located in front of the National Asian Culture Complex in Dong-gu, Gwangju. It commemorates the May 1980 Gwangju Uprising, which took place in front of the former Jeonnam Provincial Office. The square features a fountain, the Sangmu Hall, and a clock tower as symbols of the event, along with the Bell Tower of Democracy built in 2005, which rings on May 18th and Liberation Day.
spot_at_1621360.pull_quote: May 18th Democracy Square is located in front of the National Asian Culture Complex in Dong-gu, Gwangju.
paragraphs: May 18th Democracy Square is located in front of the National Asian Culture Complex in Dong-gu, Gwangju. It commemorates the May 1980 Gwangju Uprising, which took place in front of the former Jeonnam Provincial Office. The square features a fountain, the Sangmu Hall, and a clock tower as symbols of the event, along with the Bell Tower of Democracy built in 2005, which rings on May 18th and Liberation Day.

The old building that served as the Jeonnam Provincial Office was constructed in 1930 during the Japanese occupation and is now restored as the National Asian Culture Complex, designated as a national registered cultural heritage site since 1996. On May 14, 1980, students from Chonnam National University marched from the university to the square, joining forces with students from Chosun University and citizens to hold the National Democratic Grand Assembly, making it a symbolic site of the Gwangju Democratization Movement.

spot_at_126350.title: Wonhyo Temple (Gwangju)
spot_at_126350.addr: 1514-35 Mudeung-ro, Buk-gu, Gwangju, South Jeolla Province
spot_at_126350.overview: Wonhyo Temple is a traditional temple located in the majestic mountains of Mudeungsan, Gwangju, known for having the most beautiful pavilion in Korea. It is said that the temple was established by Wonhyo Daesa during the Silla period, who loved the beauty of the mountains. The name 'Wonhyoam' is derived from this history. Some say it was founded by a famous Huayan sect monk during the Goryeo period, who named it out of admiration for Wonhyo.

Some say it was founded by a famous Huayan sect monk during the Goryeo period, who named it out of admiration for Wonhyo. The subsequent history is hard to verify, but it is known that the temple regained prominence during the regency of Queen Munjeong, and it was also where the commander of the Joseon period, Yeonggyu, practiced. After being burned down during the Imjin War, it was reconstructed by Seokgyeong, who personally made the tiles for the restoration.

spot_at_127323.title: Gwangju Chung-hyo-dong Kiln Site
spot_at_127323.addr: 14 Pungamje-gil, Buk-gu, Gwangju, South Jeolla Province
spot_at_127323.overview: The kiln site located in Chung-hyo-dong, north of Mudeungsan, was used for producing celadon, buncheong, and white porcelain from the late Goryeo to the early Joseon period. The structure of the kiln includes access facilities, a firing room for placing pottery, and a chimney, resembling a connected round tomb shape. Based on records from the 'Annals of King Sejong' and the dating of excavated artifacts, it is believed to have started production around 1430.

spot_at_945477.title: Uam Historical Park
spot_at_945477.overview: Uam Historical Park is an urban neighborhood park located in Dong-gu, Daejeon, where the great Confucian scholar Uam Song Si-yeol studied during the late Joseon Dynasty. From 1991 to 1997, buildings such as Jangpan-gak, a museum, and a Confucian academy were recreated, and it was reborn as a historical park on April 17, 1998. This park was established to honor and preserve the legacy of Uam Song Si-yeol, who flourished Confucian thought in this land during the late Joseon Dynasty. It contains historically significant cultural heritage, including Namganjeongsa, where Song Si-yeol taught his disciples in his later years, and Gikukjeong, known for its architectural beauty.

spot_at_3495467.title: Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District
spot_at_3495467.overview: The Jangsaengpo Whale Culture District is a cultural center for whales established in the Jangsaengpo area of Nam-gu, Ulsan. It is a historical area where whales have inhabited since prehistoric times, and it is the only tourist district in Korea where visitors can comprehensively experience the history and culture related to whales. The district is home to various exhibition and experience facilities focused on whale ecology and whaling culture. The main facility, the Jangsaengpo Whale Museum, displays various artifacts such as whale skeletons and whaling tools, while the Whale Ecology Experience Center is the first dolphin aquarium in Korea.

The surrounding valleys are filled with bizarre rock formations and diverse tree species, preserving the mysteries of ancient times. The clear and clean valleys provide abundant water, allowing visitors to experience both mental and physical healing. Unlike other recreation forests in the country, it is divided into upper and lower recreation areas, with the upper area known for its slow-paced environment.

spot_at_126184.title: Seongnamsa Temple (Ulsan)
spot_at_126184.overview: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The name Seongnamsa is derived from the fact that it is located south of Gajisan, which is also known as Seokmyeonsan. It is said that the monk Doi, who introduced Zen Buddhism to Korea during the reign of King Heondeok (the 41st king of Silla, 809-826 AD), discovered the site of Gajisan while searching for a sacred place.
spot_at_126184.pull_quote: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism.
paragraphs: Seongnamsa Temple is located at the eastern foot of Gajisan Mountain in Deokhyeon-ri, Sangbuk-myeon, Ulju-gun, and is a branch temple of Tongdosa, the main temple of the 15th district of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The name Seongnamsa is derived from the fact that it is located south of Gajisan, which is also known as Seokmyeonsan.

The monk Doi, who introduced Zen Buddhism to Korea during the reign of King Heondeok (the 41st king of Silla, 809-826 AD), discovered the site of Gajisan while searching for a sacred place and established the temple to pray for the protection of Silla. After several reconstructions, the temple was destroyed during the Imjin War but was rebuilt in 1674 (the 15th year of King Hyeonjong) with the support of the local governor. Over the years, the temple fell into disrepair but was restored again in 1912 by Monk Uun, only to be devastated during the Korean War.

spot_at_2675068.title: National Sejong Arboretum
spot_at_2675068.overview: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city. Opened in October 2020, it is the second national arboretum following the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum, aimed at preserving and utilizing tree genetic resources by climate and vegetation types. The arboretum consists of three main areas: the Garden Exhibition Area, Plant Education Experience Area, and Community Participation Activity Area.
spot_at_2675068.pull_quote: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city.
paragraphs: The National Sejong Arboretum is the first urban national arboretum in South Korea. Adjacent to the Government Sejong Complex, it provides a space to experience nature within the city. Opened in October 2020, it is the second national arboretum following the National Baekdudaegan Arboretum, aimed at preserving and utilizing tree genetic resources by climate and vegetation types. The arboretum consists of three main areas: the Garden Exhibition Area, Plant Education Experience Area, and Community Participation Activity Area.

The Garden Exhibition Area consists of nine gardens, including a traditional Korean garden that embodies the beauty of Korean tradition, a bonsai garden, a wildflower garden, a maple garden, an amphibian observation area, an ecological forest, a clear stream garden, an iris garden, and a wall garden. The Plant Education Experience Area has 11 spaces designed for understanding and experiencing plants, including a folk plant garden, a four-season exhibition garden, a rare and specialty plant garden, a forest garden, a garden plant measuring area, a forest restoration garden, a healing garden, a hibiscus garden, a children's forest experience area, a pollinator garden, and a commemorative garden for the IFLA World Landscape Architects Congress.
The Community Participation Activity Area is designed for citizen participation and leisure activities.

paragraphs: Hyoja Gang Yeong-cheon, a member of the Jinju Gang clan, lost his father at the age of three and lived with his widowed mother, Yeon-il Jeong. At the age of seven, his mother fell ill and became bedridden. Despite his young age, Yeong-cheon showed great filial piety. While caring for his sick mother, when her condition worsened and she lost consciousness, he broke his finger on the threshold to draw blood and let it flow into her mouth, collapsing.

His mother woke up to find her son bleeding and collapsed, and after careful nursing, he was able to wake up. The plaque hanging in front of the main gate reads, 'Hyoja Eobmugang Yeong-cheon Ji Mun-gak Gang Hee 39th Year Kyungjin March 15th Entry', indicating that this Hyoja Gate was built in the 26th year of King Sukjong (March 15, 1700). The original building was lost over nearly 290 years, and it was restored in 1987.

spot_at_128064.title: Gwanggyosan
spot_at_128064.overview: Gwanggyosan (582m above sea level) stretches about 2 km north and south between the Gyeongbu Expressway and the road connecting Seoul and Suwon, located in Sang Gwanggyo-dong, Suwon. The ridge of the mountain is very tranquil and gentle, surrounded by lush trees, making it a great place for forest bathing or a cozy day hike. spot_at_1955957.overview: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who, in 1455 during the reign of King Danjong, retreated to the mountains due to their resentment over the usurpation of the throne by Suyang Daegun. paragraphs: Gueunsa Temple, located in Sagok 2-ri, Geunnam-myeon, Cheorwon-gun, is a shrine dedicated to the nine scholars who, in 1455 during the reign of King Danjong, retreated to the mountains due to their resentment over the usurpation of the throne by Suyang Daegun. These scholars (Kim Si-seup, Jo Sang-chi, Park Do, Park Jae, Park Gyu-son, Park Hyo-son, Park Cheon-son, Park In-son, Park Gye-son) dedicated their lives to the principles of integrity and loyalty.

The nine scholars lived in huts in the mountainous valleys of Geunnam-myeon, such as Yukdan-ri, Jamgok-ri, and Sagok-ri, focusing on agriculture while gathering to play Go and discuss worldly matters. However, as the times changed, they dispersed to various places. In the 9th year of King Injo's reign (1631), several scholars, including Lee Ji-yeon, gathered their intentions to build a shrine and held memorial ceremonies every spring and autumn. In 1865, during the Daewon-gun's order to abolish Confucian academies, the shrine faced destruction, but it was rebuilt in 1921 and restored again in 1977 with the help of local benefactors after being devastated during the Korean War.

spot_at_2569465.title: Yongam-ri Prehistoric Site
spot_at_2569465.addr: 1121 Yongam-ri, Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun, Gangwon Special Self-Governing Province
spot_at_2569465.overview: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun. This site is formed on the alluvial plain of the upper reaches of the Bukhan River, winding around the areas of Wirari and Yongam-ri. Excavations conducted by the Gangwon Historical and Cultural Research Institute from 2001 to 2003 revealed over 230 remains, including 176 house sites, 32 burial pits, 14 pillar-supported buildings, and 11 earthen tombs, showcasing the highest density of Bronze Age remains in the country.
spot_at_2569465.pull_quote: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun.
paragraphs: The Yongam-ri prehistoric site in Hwacheon is a large-scale village site from the Bronze Age located in Hanam-myeon, Hwacheon-gun. This site is formed on the alluvial plain of the upper reaches of the Bukhan River, winding around the areas of Wirari and Yongam-ri. Excavations conducted by the Gangwon Historical and Cultural Research Institute from 2001 to 2003 revealed over 230 remains, including 176 house sites, 32 burial pits, 14 pillar-supported buildings, and 11 earthen tombs, showcasing the highest density of Bronze Age remains in the country.

The Bronze Age settlement formed in the Yongam-ri area is evaluated as a very important site that can shed light on the lifestyle and residential development of the Bronze Age in the Bukhan River basin, as well as the diffusion routes of Bronze Age culture, dating back to at least the 10th century BC to the 6th century BC. The site is also considered to have great preservation value as it is a rare village site in East Asia. A large quantity of stone tools, including chipped stone tools made from flakes, as well as various forms of stone axes and arrowheads, have been excavated. These stone tools exhibit complete or partially completed forms typical of Bronze Age remains.

The temple stay program is divided into experiential and relaxation types.

spot_at_4096597.title: Hoengseong Catholic Church
spot_at_4096597.overview: This church showcases the modern church history of the Hoengseong area and the characteristics of post-war stone architecture. Originally, there was a chapel of Pungsuwon Catholic Church here, which was elevated to a parish in 1930, and a tiled wooden structure was built. After the original building was destroyed during the Korean War, the current stone church was constructed. The building features a Latin cross-shaped floor plan, and the interior mass space is designed as an auditorium without columns or walls.

paragraphs: This church showcases the modern church history of the Hoengseong area and the characteristics of post-war stone architecture. Originally, there was a chapel of Pungsuwon Catholic Church here, which was elevated to a parish in 1930, and a tiled wooden structure was built. After the original building was destroyed during the Korean War, the current stone church was constructed. The building features a Latin cross-shaped floor plan, and the interior mass space is designed as an auditorium without columns or walls.

The wooden truss above the main ceiling retains its original form from the time of construction. At the center of the front is an octagonal bell tower topped with a dome, housing a bell imported from France at the time of construction. Although the auxiliary buildings have changed several times, the exterior of the parish has mostly been preserved, showcasing the architectural style of the time. As a religious space where mass is still held, visitors should be mindful not to disturb the ceremonies and prayers of the congregation.

spot_at_2710737.title: Donghae Marine Resource Center
spot_at_2710737.overview: The Donghae Marine Resource Center, under the Korea Fisheries Resources Agency, works to preserve salmon, a key returning species along the East Coast, through breeding, nurturing, releasing, and creating natural spawning grounds. Over 70% of Korean salmon are born in the Namdaecheon River in Yangyang, where they grow for 3-4 years in the North Pacific before returning to spawn. However, due to river destruction, the number of returning salmon has decreased, prompting the center to perform artificial fertilization and hatch young salmon, which are then nurtured for about five months before being released into the Namdaecheon River.

However, due to river destruction, the number of returning salmon has decreased, prompting the center to perform artificial fertilization and hatch young salmon, which are then nurtured for about five months before being released into the Namdaecheon River.

The salmon ecology experience center within the facility provides detailed information about the hatching and growth process of salmon, as well as their returning routes. Visitors can observe young salmon that have hatched through artificial fertilization feeding and growing in the breeding facility. The center operates ecological experience programs, welcoming adult salmon in October-November and sending young salmon in February-March. Visitors have the opportunity to touch the returning salmon or release young salmon from a container into the river, allowing for close observation of their ecology.

The somewhat shabby yet tidy exterior reflects the passion and dedication of the owner, who has been focused on baking for over 50 years. Upon entering the bakery, the enticing aroma of freshly baked bread stimulates your appetite.

If you're unsure about what to buy among the neatly arranged breads, the squid rice bread is highly recommended. The squid rice bread is the signature menu item of New York Bakery, which won a silver medal at the 2018 'Our Rice Bread Competition'. The dough is made by mixing flour and rice flour, filled with local specialties like squid, dried radish greens, and cheese, baked to perfection with a unique flavor. Above all, its nutty and chewy texture is exceptional, with a hint of spiciness that enhances its taste.

spot_at_125826.title: Poamsan Mountain (Chungju)
spot_at_125826.overview: Poamsan, recognized as one of the 'Five Great Mountains of Joryeong' along with nearby Wolaksan, Juhulsan, and Joryeongsan, is located within Wolaksan National Park, marking the boundary between Chungju's Sangmo-myeon and Mungyeong in Gyeongsangbuk-do. It lies on the main ridge of the Baekdudaegan mountain range and connects to Wulhang Sam Bong via Haneuljae. Historically known as Hanheollyeong, Haneuljae served as a vital transportation route connecting the north and south of the Korean Peninsula until the Joryeong Gate was opened during the Joseon Dynasty.

Poamsan features a unique combination of valley and ridge hiking. Most trails start from the Mireuksaji parking lot, passing through Haneuljae to the summit of Poamsan, leading to Mansubong and Yongambong. In Mansugol Valley, visitors can dip their feet in the stream, providing a refreshing break. The rocky paths are well-maintained, with wooden steps in some areas, though it can be crowded with hikers.

paragraphs: A small path lies to the left just past the three-story stone pagoda in Mireuk-ri, Wolaksan. This path opens up to a refreshing breeze under the clear sky, surrounded by picturesque scenery of yellow pines, oak trees, and sea pines. Known as 'Haneuljae', the path leads down to a ditch that sometimes dries up due to drought, but is adorned with beautiful wildflowers like pink water lilies, deep purple swamp flowers, and yellow straw flowers. Although named Haneuljae (525m above sea level) as if it touches the sky, it is not particularly high.

Haneuljae serves as a boundary connecting Mireuk-ri in Chungju and Gwanum-ri in Mungyeong, taking about 30-40 minutes (2km) to walk from Mireuk-ri to Gwanum-ri. The rugged unpaved road leads to a smooth asphalt road at the top of Haneuljae, where the western peak of Daemisan (1,115m above sea level) comes into view. Additionally, the old temple site of Jungwon Mireuk-ri, believed to have been established during the late Silla to early Goryeo period, is located below Haneuljae.

spot_at_128006.title: Angseong Hot Spring Area
spot_at_128006.overview: The Angseong Hot Spring Area is a large carbonated hot spring town located in the vicinity of Donsan-ri and Neungam-ri in Angseong-myeon, Chungju. paragraphs: Located below the village of Zhoune in Jangcheon-ri, Gagum-myeon, Chungju, Mokgye Solbat is an area of pine trees, historically known as Mokgye Naru. This area features 100-200 year-old pine trees and serves as a resting spot for vacationers during the summer. It is a 3,800-pyeong forest composed solely of pine trees, designated as a protected area by Chungju City. Mokgye Naru has a legend associated with it, one of which states that it became a significant inland waterway during the Joseon Dynasty.

However, Mokgye Naru suffered from major fires every year, causing significant damage. In search of a solution to these fires, a geomancer visited the area and suggested a method to redirect the waterway. The villagers transported soil from the river's center to create a mound, successfully redirecting the river towards Mokgye after more than six months, and planted many pine trees on that mound. This is how the Mokgye Solbat came to be.

spot_at_129344.title: Chungju Sangdae Village
spot_at_129344.overview: Located in the heart of the Korean Peninsula, Sangdae Village in Jidang-ri, Angseong-myeon, Chungju, is a historically rich area. Once known as Jijang-ri, this mountain basin village has a deep history, having been part of the Mahan territory during the Three Han period and a battleground during the Three Kingdoms era. The only existing Goguryeo stele, the Jungwon Goguryeo Stele, is located east of the village.

Sangdae Village is famous for its production of Cheongdo peaches and is home to many skilled artisans. Seasonal festivals like the Peach Blossom Festival in spring, the Starry Night Film Festival in summer, and the Mountain Music Concert in winter bring vitality to the village.

spot_at_917225.title: Seosan Haemi Eupseong Zelkova Tree
spot_at_917225.overview: In front of the southern Jin-nam gate of Haemi Eupseong, there is a large zelkova tree estimated to be around 300 years old. Locally, it is also called 'Hoya Tree'. In the late Joseon period, there was a prison behind the tree where persecuted Catholic believers were held, and between 1790 and 1880, those imprisoned were tortured by being hung from branches extending to the east of this tree. Recognized for its historical significance, it was designated as a cultural asset of Chungcheongnam-do in 2008.

paragraphs: In front of the southern Jin-nam gate of Haemi Eupseong, there is a large zelkova tree estimated to be around 300 years old. Locally, it is also called 'Hoya Tree'.

In the late Joseon period, there was a prison behind the tree where persecuted Catholic believers were held, and between 1790 and 1880, those imprisoned were tortured by being hung from branches extending to the east of this tree. Recognized for its historical significance, it was designated as a cultural asset of Chungcheongnam-do in 2008.

Meanwhile, the eastern branch was broken by a storm in the 1940s, and the middle trunk was broken on June 26, 1969, but it has been protected and managed through several surgeries and soil improvement. Haemi Eupseong also preserves various old buildings such as the inner house, eastern government office, and guesthouse. Nearby, there are also Haemi Martyrdom Site (Yeosutgol), Haemi Confucian School, Haemi Eupseong Historical Camping Site, and Haemi Market. Additionally, the Seosan Aramegil and Haemi International Sacred Site paths pass through, making it a good idea to combine these for sightseeing.

spot_at_129184.overview: Located at the northern tip of the Taean Peninsula, Samgilpo Port is the largest harbor among several along the Daehwa Embankment. It attracts many tourists from surrounding areas and the capital region. While the taste of sashimi prepared on the spot from fishing boats may be unmatched, the flavor of sashimi made from freshly caught fish offers a unique delight only found at the western sea ports. This area is particularly known for its abundance of black sea bream, which thrive in the brackish waters where seawater and freshwater meet.

spot_at_129470.title: Buyeo Garim Fortress
spot_at_129470.overview: Garim Fortress is a mountain fortress built on Seongheung Mountain (260.1m) in the southern part of Buyeo-gun. It is strategically located between Buyeo's Sabiseong Fortress and the mouth of the Geumgang River, believed to have been constructed by King Dongseong of Baekje to protect Sabiseong. The parking lot below the fortress is only about 200m from the South Gate, making it relatively easy to enjoy the fortress's scenic views. There is also a memorial hall dedicated to those who participated in the Baekje Restoration Movement.

spot_at_125928.title: Birthplace of Lee Sang-jae
spot_at_125928.overview: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements. In the 18th year of Gojong's reign (1881), he visited Japan as a member of the Shin Sa Yu Ramdan and returned to serve as the secretary to the U.S. envoy Park Jeong-yang in the 25th year of Gojong's reign (1888). After returning from the U.S., he felt a strong need for new civilization and organized the Independence Association with Seo Jae-pil in the 2nd year of Gwangmu (1898) to lead the enlightenment of the people.

paragraphs: This is the site of the birthplace of Lee Sang-jae (1850-1927), a social activist during the late Joseon Dynasty. Lee Sang-jae joined Christianity early on and worked to awaken the national spirit through faith movements. In the 18th year of Gojong's reign (1881), he visited Japan as a member of the Shin Sa Yu Ramdan and returned to serve as the secretary to the U.S. envoy Park Jeong-yang in the 25th year of Gojong's reign (1888). After returning from the U.S., he felt a strong need for new civilization and organized the Independence Association with Seo Jae-pil in the 2nd year of Gwangmu (1898) to lead the enlightenment of the people.

In 1927, when the nationalist and socialist factions formed a united front to organize the New Korean Association with the goal of fighting against Japan, he was elected as the founding president. His works include the essay collections 'Young People' and 'The Foundation of the Nation for Young People'. The teacher's birthplace is a thatched house with an anchae (main house) and sarangchae (guest house), consisting of four rooms in the front and two on the side, with a gate featuring a raised design. The main house was built around 1800, and the guest house was constructed around 1926, but the original building was destroyed in 1955, and the current structure was restored in 1972 and 1980.

spot_at_129457.title: Shinseongni Reed Field
spot_at_129457.overview: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and dramas, including 'Joint Security Area (JSA)' and 'Kingdom', due to its beautiful scenery. The sunlight shimmering on the waves of the Geumgang River creates a mystical harmony, and in winter, it serves as a habitat for migratory birds such as swans and teal, making it a popular spot for nature study and photography.
spot_at_129457.pull_quote: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea.
paragraphs: Shinseongni Reed Field is a vast reed field formed at the confluence of the Geumgang River and the West Sea, recognized as one of the four major reed fields in Korea. It has been used as a filming location for various movies and dramas, including 'Joint Security Area (JSA)' and 'Kingdom', due to its beautiful scenery. The sunlight shimmering on the waves of the Geumgang River creates a mystical harmony, and in winter, it serves as a habitat for migratory birds such as swans and teal, making it a popular spot for nature study and photography.

In particular, since the completion of the Geumgang River embankment in 1990, a large freshwater lake has been created nearby, attracting even more winter migratory birds. The reed field also showcases different colors and charms in each season, and it's delightful to experience the subtly different sounds of the reeds in the wind throughout the year. Observing the reed crab, which lives in the reed field, adds another layer of enjoyment. At the entrance, there is a reed experience center where you can learn more about reeds and the history and uses of the reed fields that were once much larger before agricultural land development.

paragraphs: Maechang Park is a park created to commemorate the famous female writer Lee Mae-chang, who is known alongside Hwang Jin-yi and Heo Nan-seol-heon from the Joseon Dynasty. Lee Mae-chang (1573-1610) was a female poet during the reign of King Seonjo, known by the names Gyesaeng or Hyanggeum, with the courtesy name Cheonhyang and the pen name Mae-chang. Born as the daughter of Lee Tang-jong in Hyeon-ri, Buan, she excelled in poetry and was also skilled in music, particularly playing the geomungo.

Buan County has created a cultural park featuring a stone monument inscribed with Lee Mae-chang's poetry, along with a forest, Mae-chang Theme Exhibition Hall, Wetland Park, Buan Cultural Center, and Yu Hee-gyeong Plaza. Additionally, there are facilities for children, walking paths, and basketball courts. The park is adorned with trees and flowers, and sculptures and resting areas have been installed throughout the walking paths. At night, the park is illuminated, allowing for a charming evening stroll. The Buan Masil Festival is held in May at Maechang Park.

paragraphs: Jinan Hyanggyo was established in 1414 (the 14th year of King Taejong) to enshrine the spirits of virtuous scholars and to educate and enlighten local residents. It was destroyed during the Imjin War and rebuilt in 1601 (the 34th year of King Seonjo), and relocated to its current site in 1636 (the 14th year of King Injo). The existing buildings include the Daeseongjeon, Myeongnyundang, Beonandan, and Seojae, where the spirits of five sages, four Confucian scholars from the Song Dynasty, and eighteen scholars from Korea are enshrined.

The Daeseongjeon is a place where the spirits of Confucian scholars, including Confucius, are honored. It has a scale of three bays in the front and two bays on the side, with a gable roof that resembles the character '人' when viewed from the side. Rituals are held in spring and autumn, and during the first and fifteenth days of the month, incense is offered. The collection includes 95 types of printed books and 11 types of manuscripts, totaling 106 types and 198 volumes.

spot_at_128973.title: Jinan Eunsusa Cheongsil Pear Tree
spot_at_128973.addr: Dongchon-ri, Maryeong-myeon, Jinan-gun, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province
spot_at_128973.overview: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains. The leaves are oval-shaped with serrated edges, and both sides are hairless and firm. The fruit is brown or green and ripens to yellow in the fall. The Cheongsil pear tree growing in the Eunsusa Temple in Jinan is estimated to be over 640 years old. The tree has a unique appearance, with a large trunk splitting into four branches at the top, supporting the upper part.
spot_at_128973.pull_quote: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains.
paragraphs: The Cheongsil pear tree is a species similar to the sandol pear tree, growing near homes or in the mountains. The leaves are oval-shaped with serrated edges, and both sides are hairless and firm. The fruit is brown or green and ripens to yellow in the fall. The Cheongsil pear tree growing in the Eunsusa Temple in Jinan is estimated to be over 640 years old.

The tree has a unique appearance, with a large trunk splitting into four branches at the top, supporting the upper part. This area is influenced by the terrain, and when the wind blows, the firm leaves of the Cheongsil pear tree shake and create an indescribable sound. Additionally, in winter, if water is placed next to the base of the Cheongsil pear tree, icicles can form upside down towards the tips of the branches. The Cheongsil pear tree is a native Korean species, and there are not many left today, making large trees especially rare and designated as a natural monument. The Eunsusa Cheongsil pear tree is currently surrounded by a fence, with an information sign installed nearby.

spot_at_128807.title: Gocheonamho (Migratory Bird Habitat)
spot_at_128807.addr: Gocheonam-ro, Hwangsan-myeon, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_128807.overview: Gocheonamho is the largest reed habitat in South Korea. The Gocheonam reed fields host rare birds such as the black stork and eagles, as well as 90% of the world's migratory swans that perform spectacular dances during winter. A total of 54 bird species (excluding unidentified species) have been observed, making it the largest migratory bird habitat in the country, with 33 species of waterfowl, 5 species of raptors, and 16 other bird species.

spot_at_231919.title: Haenam Myeongnyang Battle Monument
spot_at_231919.addr: 34 Usuyoungan-gil, Munnam-myeon, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_231919.overview: The Haenam Myeongnyang Battle Monument was erected to honor Admiral Yi Sun-sin for his victory in the Battle of Myeongnyang in 1597. The inscription was written in 1686, and the monument was erected by Park Sin-joo, the naval commander of Jeolla Province, in 1688. The monument features a rectangular base with a body and a headstone adorned with clouds and dragons. The inscription records Admiral Yi's efforts to regroup his navy after the Battle of Chilcheollyang and his victory over the Japanese forces using the swift currents between Usuyoung and Jindo.

spot_at_1624224.pull_quote: Kim Nam-joo is a representative figure of Korean national literature, known as a 'warrior poet' who passionately advocated for social change and a 'national poet' who awakened the Korean literary world with his revolutionary voice. He was also…
paragraphs: Kim Nam-joo is a representative figure of Korean national literature, known as a 'warrior poet' who passionately advocated for social change and a 'national poet' who awakened the Korean literary world with his revolutionary voice. He was also a revolutionary poet who spent a decade in prison fighting against dictatorship. Born in 1945 in Bonghak-ri, Haenam-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City, he attended Samhwa Elementary School and Haenam Middle School before enrolling in Gwangju Ilgo, but he dropped out in opposition to exam-oriented education.

During his time in university, he participated in the 'Three-Term Constitutional Amendment Opposition Movement' and produced the first underground newspapers 'Hamsung' and 'Gobal' in the country during the anti-Yushin movement, which led to an 8-month prison sentence and his expulsion from university. In 1974, he debuted in the literary world with works like 'Jinhonga' in 'Creation and Criticism' and later formed the 'People's Culture Research Institute' with writers like Hwang Sok-yong. In 1978, he was active as a 'warrior' in the strongest underground organization against Yushin, 'Namminjeon', until he was arrested with his comrades in October the following year.

spot_at_126637.title: Osan (Gurye)

spot_at_126637.overview: Osan is recorded in the Bongseongji as 'the shape of the rock is outstanding, resembling Geumgangsan, and has been called 'Little Geumgang' since ancient times.' spot_at_126767.title: Dangmol Spring
spot_at_126767.addr: 3-2 Jangsu-gil, Masang-myeon, Gurye-gun, Gwangju Metropolitan City
spot_at_126767.overview: Sangsa Village is recognized as one of the longest-living villages in the country, along with Yangcheon Village in Ganjeon-myeon, Gurye-gun. The locals attribute their longevity to the clean environment of the Simsan Valley and 'Dangmol Spring'. Dangmol Spring is renowned for its exceptional health benefits, with locals claiming that 'the water from the roots of medicinal herbs in Jirisan flows here.' In 1986, a water quality test by a preventive medicine team from Korea University found it to be the best water in the country, with no E. coli detected. According to the local Kim clan, their ancestor discovered Dangmol Spring while searching for a good location in Jeolla Province during the late Joseon period.

paragraphs: The underwater tomb of King Munmu, the 30th monarch of Silla (reigned 661-681), offers a glimpse into the creative thinking of the Silla people. Located 200m from the sea off Bonggilli in the East Sea, it is exposed above sea level, measuring approximately 35m east-west, 36m north-south, and 5.3m in height. King Munmu succeeded his father, King Muyeol, in defeating Goguryeo and preventing Tang invasions, achieving the unification of the Three Kingdoms. He also established central government offices such as the Ministry of Military and the Ministry of Rites.

King Munmu, who unified the Three Kingdoms, requested that his body be cremated in a Buddhist manner and that his ashes be buried in the East Sea to prevent invasions by Japanese pirates. This rock is known as Daewangam or Daewang Rock, and the underwater royal tomb is unique in the world. paragraphs: This mural tomb, excavated in January 1985 by the Cultural Heritage Administration and Daegu University, is designated as a historic site and is a valuable resource both academically and culturally. The construction date of this tomb is estimated to be around 539 AD based on the inscription 'Gimi Jungmyo Sanginmyeong' found on the southern wall of the tomb's chamber. The internal structure is a stone chamber tomb with an entrance, leading to the chamber where the body is enshrined.

The chamber measures approximately 3.5m east-west and 2m north-south, with walls that slightly taper towards the top, and the ceiling is completed with two large flat stones. The murals cover all walls and the sides of the chamber, except for the ceiling, with particularly strong warrior figures painted on the left and right walls of the entrance. Notably, the warrior figure on the west wall, holding a snake, is interpreted as a guardian of this tomb.

There is a story involving a tiger and a monk, where Monk Duun saved a tiger caught by a hairpin around its neck, and in gratitude, the tiger offered the daughter of the local lord, Yu Seok. However, Monk Duun returned the daughter to Seorabeol, and in gratitude, Yu Seok placed an iron bridge in the stream leading to Heebangsa Temple.

spot_at_250281.title: Gyeongju Inwang-dong Temple Site
spot_at_250281.overview: The Inwang-dong Temple Site in Gyeongju is believed to be the former location of Inyongsa Temple. Mentioned in the 'Samguk Yusa' (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms), Inyongsa was built to pray for the well-being of Kim In-mun (629–694), the second son of King Muyeol of Silla. According to historical records, after Goguryeo fell, Tang China attempted to conquer Silla and imprisoned Kim In-mun, who was staying in Tang. The people of Silla opened a Avalokitesvara ritual to pray for his return, but when Kim In-mun died in 694 (the 3rd year of King Hyoso's reign) on his way back home, the ritual was converted into an Amitabha sanctuary to pray for his rebirth in the Pure Land. Inyongsa is the first recorded temple in Silla built for a private individual rather than a monk or royal family member, reflecting the religious practices of the time. Excavations were conducted four times between 2002 and 2011 by the National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage. It features a typical Silla twin-pagoda temple layout, alongside a rare '亞' (A-shaped) building site, pagoda sites, a main hall site, lecture hall site, corridor site, lotus pond, and a well.

paragraphs: The Gyeongju Inwang-dong Temple Site in Gyeongju is believed to be the site of Inyongsa Temple. Featured in the 'Samguk Yusa', Inyongsa was a temple built to pray for the well-being of Kim In-mun (629–694), the second son of King Muyeol. According to records, after the fall of Goguryeo, Tang China attempted to conquer Silla and imprisoned Kim In-mun, who was staying in Tang.

The people of Silla held a Gwaneum (Avalokitesvara) ritual praying for his return, but when Kim In-mun died in 694 (the 3rd year of King Hyoso's reign) while returning home, they changed it to a Mita (Amitabha) ritual to pray for his peaceful afterlife. Inyongsa is the first temple in Silla built for a private individual rather than a monk or a monarch, showing the form of faith at the time. Excavations were carried out in four phases from 2002 to 2011 by the National Gyeongju Research Institute of Cultural Heritage. Featuring a typical Silla twin-pagoda layout, a rare '亞'-shaped building site, pagoda sites, main hall site, lecture hall site, corridor site, lotus pond, and well have been identified.

spot_at_2599775.title: Sangju Heossi Silk Fabric
spot_at_2599775.overview: Heossi Silk is carrying on the 5th generation of traditional silk weaving from silkworm cocoons, one of the key specialties of Sangju, a region famously known for its 'three whites' (rice, silk, and dried persimmons). The workshop relocated to its current site in 2002, actively opening its spacious 3,000-pyeong grounds to operate a reservation-only silk weaving experience center. spot_fo_2838772.title: Gyeongju Milmyeon Main Branch
spot_fo_2838772.overview: Milmyeon (wheat noodles) is a dish created by North Korean refugees who evacuated to Busan during the Korean War. The Gyeongju Milmyeon Main Branch inherited this noodle-making technique to faithfully recreate the authentic taste of traditional milmyeon. The noodles are freshly kneaded and pulled upon ordering, served in a broth simmered for 24 hours with Korean beef bones, medicinal herbs, and various vegetables. A standout feature here is that ordering milmyeon comes with charcoal-grilled iron-griddle bulgogi. Other menu items include spicy seasoned Bibim Milmyeon, handmade dumplings, and a whole plate of iron-griddle bulgogi.

paragraphs: Motjae is a pond located on the summit of Jisan Mountain to the west of Naecheon-ri, Yulgok-myeon, Hapcheon-gun. While some say it is a crater lake formed by a volcanic explosion, it is presumed to have been created by natural subsidence. A plant called watershield (sunchae) grows naturally here. In the past, this plant was considered a miraculous remedy for leprosy, skin diseases, and jaundice, prompting many patients to visit in search of medicinal herbs to cure their illnesses. It is also said that nearby residents used to gather on the surrounding lawn to divide into teams and build camaraderie through folk wrestling (ssireum) matches.

Additionally, during the Imjin War, Japanese troops camped here and engaged in battle with our righteous army stationed at Baengmasanseong Fortress opposite. The surrounding Jisan Park, located just north of Cheonjimot Pond, is a community amenity featuring an octagonal pavilion, lawns, and shady trees where local residents enjoy picnics. Cheonjibong Peak, at the summit of Cheonjimot, offers breathtaking panoramic views in all directions, and on the first full moon of the lunar new year, residents burn large moon-welcoming fires (daljip) to pray for a bountiful harvest and peace. Known as Dalmaji-bong (Moon-gazing Peak), it is a naturally occurring resort deeply rooted in history and scenic beauty.

spot_at_2611161.title: Oepo Port, Geoje
spot_at_2611161.overview: Designated as a national fishing port in December 1971 and currently managed by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Oepo Port spans 0.8 km in width with an inner harbor depth of 8m and outer harbor depth of 22m. As the nation's premier Pacific cod distribution center—accounting for over 30% of the country's cod supply—the port comes alive every day at 10 AM with the booming voices of auctioneers at the Oepo-ri fish market. Packed with fresh cod, it is a wonderful place to enjoy invigorating cod soup.

spot_at_128947.title: Hwangsan Village Traditional Stone-Mud Walls, Geochang
spot_at_128947.overview: The ancient stone-mud walls of Hwangsan Village in Geochang enclose traditional houses belonging to the Geochang Sin clan lineage. The village preserves houses built from the late Joseon Dynasty to the modern era, offering a glimpse of a traditional Korean settlement. Large natural stones are stacked at the base without mortar to ensure good drainage, topped with alternating layers of small stones and clay. Most walls are capped with traditional Korean tile roofing (hansik giwa). The gently curving walls harmonize with historic houses to create a serene landscape.

spot_at_127042.title: Mireukdo Island, Tongyeong
spot_at_127042.overview: Mireukdo is an island south of Tongyeong connected to the mainland by two bridges and an undersea tunnel. Its highlight is the Sanyang Coastal Circular Road, famous for offering the ultimate Hallyudo marine scenery with beautiful coastal curves, hills, and quiet fishing ports. Donam-dong, the starting point of the circular road, features marina resorts and cruise terminals heading to nearby Hansando, Bijindo, Maemuldo, and Geoje Haegeumgang. Further south, Dala Park features benches and pavilions for viewing breathtaking sunsets over the southern sea. Yonghwasan Mountain in the center houses Yonghwasa and Miraesa temples, and walking the quiet forest trail between them is a must-do experience.

Mireukdo's coastal highlight, the Sanyang Circular Road, is famous for offering breathtaking views of the Hallyu archipelago, featuring stunning coastline curves, hills, and tranquil harbor scenery.

Donam-dong, the starting point, features marina resorts for water sports and cruise terminals offering trips to nearby Hansando, Bijindo, Maemuldo, and Geoje Haegeumgang, along with lodging and amenities. Dala Park on the south side of the road offers benches, resting areas, and a pavilion to enjoy dazzling sunset views over the South Sea. Meanwhile, Yonghwasan Mountain in the center features Yonghwasa Temple to the north and Miraesa Temple to the south; walking the tranquil hiking trail connecting both temples is a true highlight of Mireukdo tourism.

spot_at_126660.title: Mireukdo Tourist Zone, Tongyeong
spot_at_126660.overview: Mireukdo is an island within Hallyeohaesang National Park, serving as a hub for South Sea marine tourism and connected to the mainland via Chungmugyo Bridge. Designated as a special tourist zone, it offers diverse leisure opportunities. A major landmark is Mireuksan Mountain, rising in the center of the island. Visitors can take the Hallyudo Viewing Cable Car completed in 2008 to the summit for panoramic views of the archipelago. Though not exceptionally tall, Mireuksan is celebrated for its lush forests and clear streams, showcasing royal azaleas in spring and brilliant foliage in autumn.

spot_at_591798.title: Hagosudong Beach
spot_at_591798.overview: Located in the sea northeast of Seongsanpo at the eastern tip of Jeju Island, Hagosudong Beach on the volcanic island of Udo is divided into two sections by a rocky coastline exposed in the center. The total length of the beach is about 400m, with basalt reefs exposed around 100m and 200m–300m to the east, and dune layers developed in the background. The beach was formed by the accumulation of materials transported by coastal currents. Until the 1970s, anchovy fishing using traditional 'huritgeum' (haul nets) took place here.

spot_at_591866.overview: Located in Hallim-eup, Jeju-si, Geumneung Beach is directly connected to Hyeopjae Beach, a popular spot on the western coast. While it shares a similar landscape with its neighboring beach—featuring a sea that looks like dissolved blue paint, the cute-shaped Biyangdo Island, and soft sandy shores—its charm lies in being less crowded and more leisurely. The parking lot connects directly to the beach, making it hassle-free to carry your belongings. The newly built shower facility is equipped with hot water showers for added convenience. When visiting this place, we recommend timing your visit to match the low tide.

When the seawater recedes far out, a wide, fine sandy beach is revealed. Natural pools with shallow depths, perfect for young children to play in, are formed in various spots. Seaweed and small sea snails left behind by the receding seawater naturally become toys for the children. Thanks to this, you can have a fun time even if you visit without any special preparation. However, since crushed seashell fragments are mixed with the sand at the beach entrance, wearing water shoes is strongly recommended. (Source: Visit Jeju Website)

Stepping into a building designed to replicate the old Seoul Station, visitors are greeted with miniature buildings of various themes and displays of vintage items. Walking through scenes of old downtown areas, moon villages, retro dance halls, tea rooms, and comic book shops modeled after traditional marketplaces, older generations can reminisce while younger generations who haven't experienced those times can imagine the lives their parents once lived.

spot_at_601489.title: Seogwipo Marine Provincial Park
spot_at_601489.overview: This is a marine provincial park centered around the coast of Seogwipo-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Recognized as one of the 75 scenic views of Seogwipo, it is well-known as the quintessential Seogwipo coastal scenic spot, featuring coastal cliffs spanning about seventyri east and west around Seogwipo City harmonizing with islands floating on blue waves. Boasting beautiful scenery, it is the southern limit habitat for globally rare distylium trees (machilus thunbergii) and the natural monument black pigeon.
spot_at_601489.pull_quote: This is a marine provincial park centered around the coast of Seogwipo-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Recognized as one of the 75 scenic views of Seogwipo, it is well-known...
paragraphs: This is a marine provincial park centered around the coast of Seogwipo-si, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province. Recognized as one of the 75 scenic views of Seogwipo, it is well-known as the quintessential Seogwipo coastal scenic spot, featuring coastal cliffs spanning about seventyri east and west around Seogwipo City harmonizing with islands floating on blue waves. Boasting beautiful scenery, it is the southern limit habitat for globally rare distylium trees and the natural monument black pigeon.

It also represents the biodiversity of southern marine species as a site featuring prominent geological columnar joints and numerous new or unrecorded species of Korean endemic marine life with high academic value. To maintain ecological order through marine ecosystem resource conservation and create new tourism trends by maximizing resource utilization, Seogwipo Marine City Park was converted into Seogwipo Marine Provincial Park in January 2007. It is particularly well-known as a wonderful spot for sunrises and sunsets. Furthermore, located at the entrance of Cheonjeyeon Waterfall, the park serves as a relaxing station for those returning after fully absorbing the beauty of the waterfall.

spot_at_660972.title: Hado-ri Migratory Bird Habitat
spot_at_660972.overview: Located in Hado-ri, Gujwa-eup, Jeju-si, this migratory bird habitat is adjacent to the sea and boasts abundant nutrient-rich prey and wetland plants, making it an optimal region for migratory birds to spend the winter. Designated as a natural monument, the area welcomes about 30 species of migratory birds every year, including the black-faced spoonbill—of which only about 1,600 remain worldwide—as well as natural monuments like swans, falcons, and kestrels, and the Ministry of Environment's endangered wild animal, the osprey.
